If d is positive, find two real roots via x = (-b ± √d) / (2a). If d equals zero, there’s one repeated root; if negative, the equation has complex solutions. Always double-check your calculations step by step.

Then, substitute these values back into f(x) to find the corresponding y-coordinates, which represent potential maxima, minima, or inflection points.
